notes: `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` section 10.1, Task 2: verify `T↑ ⊆ T` under `V = E ∘ E`. Global schema `{E}` (binary), local schema `{V}` (ternary) with the LAV view `V(a, b, c) ↔ E(a, b) ∧ E(b, c)`. The programs and the constraint are exactly Task 1's; only the claim differs, from the equality of Example4002 to this containment.

The source documents the reformulations task document (sha256 `32a3ac6b428d851f0aaa4fb7acdbf2fe4ad5dacca93ee118837888ff91b7a1c6`) and `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` (sha256 `796ff97c082c6fc70e75a60c0dd40ec0680b738d7184a8b8aefea8c681b3ebff`) carry the same section 10.1 text, so both name this task.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example4003.lean` states the PDF's two Datalog programs, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the two compiled commands one after the other, renames the generated snapshots `T_1` and `TUp_1` to the auxiliary input names `T_aux` and `TUp_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` as the view constraint and `inputPost` as the claim `TUp ⊆ T` and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence.

The transitive closure is the PDF's verbatim left-linear program. The reference encoding replaced it by an accelerated variant carrying the derived rules `T(x, y) :- E(x, z), E(z, y)` and `T(x, y) :- E(x, z), E(z, w), T(w, y)`, which has the same least fixpoint but advances two edges per iteration; the fidelity module states that variant as a second Datalog program and separates the two by one immediate-consequence step on `E = {(0, 1), (1, 2)}`, where the verbatim program derives only the two edges while the variant already derives `(0, 2)`. A regression to the variant fails that test.
Expected verdict valid: `TUp` collects exactly the paths of even length at least two, and every path lies in `T`. Nothing is certified in this pass, so the classification stays `unknown`.

Reference encoding for intent only: the retired corpus case Example4003, an `IndexAlphaName` hand-written input in the earlier single-level framework carrying the accelerated variant. Nothing is copied from it.

The the reference encoding's certified invariant into four level-0 clauses over the computed prophecy schema, mapping its previous-round copies `T_2`/`TUp_2` onto this encoding's `T_aux`/`TUp_aux`: `(op_zTUp ⊆ op_zT)`, `(oa_zTUp ⊆ oa_zT)`, `(op_zV ⊆ π[0,1,3] (σ[#1 = #2] ((op_zE × op_zE))))` and `(π[0,1,3] (σ[#1 = #2] ((op_zE × op_zE))) ⊆ op_zV)`. A hint, not evidence.

That invariant does not close over the re-encoded input, so the classification stays `unknown`. The initialization obligation of `(op_zTUp ⊆ op_zT)` is not valid, and it is the first obligation the build fails on. At the loop head the preprocessed precondition gives `T_aux = ∅`, `T = E ∪ π[0,3] (σ[#1 = #2] ((E × T_aux)))`, so `T = E`, while `TUp_aux = ∅` and `TUp = π[0,2] (V) ∪ π[0,4] (σ[#2 = #3] ((V × TUp_aux)))`, so `TUp` already holds every length-two path; on `E = {(0, 1), (1, 2)}` the pair `(0, 2)` is in `TUp` and not in `T`. This is the desynchronization the reference encoding avoided by running an accelerated transitive closure, and its own note says the PDF-faithful pairing this corpus now carries admits no quantifier-free invariant. Finding a different invariant is left open.
title: Containment of the path-view reformulation in transitive closure
explanation: This case uses the same global program (right-linear transitive closure T of E) and the same local reformulation (TUp, chaining the length-two path view V = E ∘ E) as Example4002, but weakens the postcondition from equality to a one-directional (forward) containment, TUp ⊆ T: every pair the view-chaining reformulation derives should also be a transitive-closure pair. The header states the expected verdict is valid, since TUp collects exactly the even-length-at-least-two paths, all of which lie in T; no certificate exists yet for this pass, so the classification stays unknown.
preInWords: The precondition states that V equals the set of length-two paths through E, i.e. V = E ∘ E with the midpoint kept.
postInWords: The postcondition asserts TUp ⊆ T, that every pair produced by the view-chaining reformulation is also produced by transitive closure.
